claims.claim_text: In females, macroadenomas were markedly attenuated by VF- (1.33 ± 0.23 mean ± SE; P < 0.05), but not by caloric restriction (2.35 ± 0.25; P = 0.71), as compared with ad libitum (2.50 ± 0.34).
hs-CRP decreased by geometric mean 0.92 mg/L (0.53-1.31, P < 0.001) in the diet

adult female mice maintained under 40% caloric restriction (CR) did not exhibit aging-related increases in oocyte aneuploidy, chromosomal misalignment, meiotic spindle abnormalities, or mitochondrial dysfunction
Mice under 40% caloric restriction showed reversal in weight gain and recovered insulin sensitivity, fasting glucose, and insulin levels.
In males, however, caloric restriction (1.71 ± 0.26; P < 0.01), but not VF- (2.94 ± 0.42; P = 0.29), reduced macroadenomas, as compared with ad libitum males (3.47 ± 0.30).
In females, both VF- (P = 0.05) and caloric restriction (P < 0.01) improved survival, but not in male mice (P = 0.15).
Bone-formation indices were lower, whereas bone-resorption indices were higher (p < .01 for all) in CR versus normal diet mice.
CR mice had 52% and 88% lower serum leptin at 6 and 12 weeks of age
CR mice had 33% and 39% lower serum IGF-1 at 6 and 12 weeks of age
bone marrow adiposity was elevated dramatically in CR versus normal diet mice (p < .05)
Neutrophil counts decreased by 0.31 × 10(9)/L (0.09-0.54, P = 0.006) in the diet
IL-6 decreased by 0.34 pg/mL (0.13-0.55, P = 0.001) in the diet
proteome half-lives of old hearts significantly increased after short-term CR (30%)
inguinal fat was significantly increased by CR at 66 weeks and 106 weeks.
mice were submitted to 1 mo of 40% caloric restriction (2 g/day of HFD).
As compared with ad libitum, VF- and caloric restriction reduced macroadenomas to a similar extent (P < 0.05), but only caloric restriction significantly improved survival (P < 0.05).
